summary: The root حرر (Hrr) primarily signifies setting free, emancipating, or liberating someone or something from bondage, slavery, or restriction.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.gloss: He freed, liberated; emancipated; He freed a neck

parts.t: for the worship of God and the service of the mosque or oratory:

headwords.def: حرّر حرر , inf. n. تَحْرِيرٌ , He freed, liberated, or emancipated, a slave. (A, Mgh, Msb.) And حرّر رَقَبَةً He freed a neck [i. e. a slave ]. (S, K.) Also He set apart a child for the worship of God and the service of the mosque or oratory: (S, TA:) or he devoted him to the service of the church as long as he should live, so that he could not relinquish it while he retained his religion. (TA.) Also, inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He made a writing &c. accurate, or exact; (S, K;) he made a writing beautiful, or elegant, and free from defects, by forming its characters rightly, and rectifying its faults : (A:) he wrote a writing well, or elegantly, and accurately, or exactly; (TK;) he wrote well, or elegantly : (KL:) and he made an account, or a reckoning,

headwords.def: حَرُورٌ حرور , of the fem. gender, (Msb,) A hot wind, (Msb,) in the night or in the day; (AA, Fr, Msb;) as also سَمُومٌ : (AA, Msb:) or the former is a hot wind in the night, and sometimes in the day; (AO, S, K;) and the latter, a hot wind in the day, and sometimes in the night: (AO, S:) or the former, a hot wind in the night; like the latter in the day: (S:) or the former, in the day; the latter being in the night; accord. to Ru-beh, as said to AO: (Msb:) pl. حَرَائِرُ . حُرُورٌ حرور : see حَرٌّ .
